title: Pioneer Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
next_steps: Redwood to send onboarding checklist and architecture diagram (Sofia)
Schedule SE deep-dive for performance benchmarks and sample workload (Liam)
Customer to share data classification and retention requirements (Emily)
Agree pilot start date and success criteria by next Friday
action_items: Sofia - Send onboarding checklist + links to docs (due 2027-04-07)
Liam - Prepare benchmark plan and sample prompt set (due 2027-04-09)
Carlos - Provide network diagram and confirm VPC peering options (due 2027-04-08)
Emily - Confirm pilot participants and timeline (due 2027-04-06)
summary: Kickoff for Pioneer Health onboarding. Covered goals, timeline, integration options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security requirements (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), pilot success criteria, and next steps to share docs and schedule a technical deep-dive. Action items assigned for checklist, benchmark plan, and network details.
topics: Deployment modes: hosted vs dedicated vs private
transcript: [00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're on for an hour, is that still ok?
[00:12] Jordan Miles: Yup that's good. we have Aisha, Carlos, Emily and me. excited to get this rolling
[00:20] Maya Chen: Quick intros from Redwood side — i'm Maya, i'll be your CSM and i'll help with onboarding coordination
[00:28] Liam O'Connor: Liam, SE, i'll handle the technical deep dives and benchmarks
[00:34] Aisha Khan: Great, i'm Aisha, VP Product. main goal for us is to integrate summarization and triage workflows into our patient support queue
[00:45] Sofia Patel: Perfect. the plan today — align on goals, timelines, what success looks like, then we cover integration options and security briefly, and finish with next steps
[01:10] Carlos Ramirez: One thing up front, we are pretty strict on data residency and can't send PHI to third-party hosted systems without a BAA — is that something Redwood supports?

[01:25] Sofia Patel: Yes, we support Private deployments and can do Dedicated with data isolation; we also have BAA customers — i'll share the legal pack. quick note, some product names may get transcribed weirdly, apologies if i say Redwood Dedicated as 'red wood dedicat' in the notes
[01:50] Jordan Miles: Cool, the requirement is that any PHI must stay in our VPC or on-prem. for pilot we can use de-identified data but long term we need private option

[02:08] Liam O'Connor: From a technical pov, we can support both. For private we do a control-plane & data-path separation; we'll need network details for peering/firewall rules. Carlos, can you share your current infra?

[02:22] Carlos Ramirez: We're primarily on AWS, accounts split by environment; we'll share a network diagram. curious about latency targets — our triage workflow needs sub-700ms median for short summaries
[02:40] Sofia Patel: Good to capture. success metric you mentioned earlier Aisha?
[02:46] Aisha Khan: Reducing time agents spend per ticket by 30% first quarter after rollout, accuracy of classification at 90%+ as measured on our eval set
[03:00] Maya Chen: We'll capture that as pilot success criteria: accuracy >90% on your prompts, latency within your SLO, and integration with your ticketing system
[03:14] Emily Nguyen: Timeline — we want a pilot in the next 4 weeks if possible. is that feasible?

[03:20] Liam O'Connor: Straightforward if we get sample prompts and a small eval set. for Dedicated or Hosted trial we can stand up quickly — Private will need more time for network setup and approvals
[03:36] Jordan Miles: For pilot we prefer Redwood Hosted with de-identified data to move fast, then move to Dedicated/Private for prod — is that typical?
[03:45] Sofia Patel: That's our common pattern, yes. Hosted to validate UX and quality, then Dedicated/Private for production compliance
[04:02] Aisha Khan: On security, we need to confirm SOC2 Type II and whether logs/audit trail can be exported to our SIEM
[04:10] Maya Chen: Redwood has SOC2; we'll share the report under NDA. logs and audit exports are supported — we can stream to your CloudWatch/Datadog via our integration or provide S3 deliveries
[04:25] Carlos Ramirez: KMS? We use AWS KMS and we'd want customer-managed keys for encryption at rest
[04:31] Liam O'Connor: We integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated deployments. for hosted there are key management options and we can discuss bring-your-own-key for certain tiers
[04:48] Jordan Miles: Ok makes sense. what about single sign-on and RBAC? we need SSO with SAML and scoped roles for developers vs ops
[04:57] Maya Chen: SSO/SAML is supported, and we have RBAC roles that integrate with SCIM for provisioning. i'll share the admin guide
[05:08] Emily Nguyen: Integration surface — we want Redwood to push summarizations into our Zendesk and also call an internal webhook. what are the typical ways to do that?

[05:19] Liam O'Connor: Two common patterns: 1) Push from Redwood via webhooks to your endpoint, or 2) you call Redwood API from your backend and orchestrate it. For lower latency and tighter control many teams prefer calling the API from their VPC-connected service
[05:38] Carlos Ramirez: If we do Private, could we host the inference inside our VPC and keep control of egress?
[05:45] Liam O'Connor: Yep, private deployments can be inside customer-controlled networks. We'll need to coordinate peering and security groups; that'll take a bit of ops time to approve
[06:02] Aisha Khan: About models — do you provide a model catalog or do we bring our own?

[06:08] Sofia Patel: We have a model catalog with Redwood-verified open models and variants. You can also bring your fine-tuned models for deployment. for pilot, we usually start with a robust open model and optionally test a fine-tuned variant later
[06:25] Jordan Miles: Budget question — what's the typical cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated? we need rough numbers to talk to finance
[06:33] Sofia Patel: Hosted is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated has a reserved capacity commit and is cheaper per-token at scale. i'll send a pricing sheet — exact numbers vary by model family and throughput
[06:48] Emily Nguyen: Great. Another ops note: we have strict egress controls, so if using hosted we'll need IP allowlist and a secure tunnel option
[06:58] Liam O'Connor: We support IP allowlists and can do private link / secure peering in some cloud regions. we'll note the regions supported so you can confirm
[07:12] Carlos Ramirez: For benchmark planning, what's the best way to provide sample traffic? do you want raw logs, or a curated prompt set?

[07:20] Liam O'Connor: Curated prompt set + representative latency-critical short prompts is best. we also accept anonymized logs if you can sanitize them. we'll run perf tests against your distributions and give recommendations on batching and quantization
[07:40] Sofia Patel: I'll attach a template for the eval prompt set after this call. it's usually 200-500 prompts representative of your top flows
[07:52] Aisha Khan: Onboard success — who from Redwood will be primary contact?
[07:58] Maya Chen: I'll be primary CSM; Sofia is the AE, and Liam is the SE for technical work. Emily, you'll be the project manager on your side
[08:10] Emily Nguyen: Sounds good. one more question: retention — we need logs kept for 12 months for audits, is that supported?
[08:19] Maya Chen: Yes, audit logs retention can be configured; longer retention is an add-on but it's common for enterprise customers
[08:30] Jordan Miles: Ok good. moving to pilot success criteria — recap please so it's documented

[08:36] Sofia Patel: Pilot success: 1) classification accuracy >=90% on your eval set, 2) median latency <700ms on short prompts, 3) integration with Zendesk and webhook working end-to-end, 4) stakeholder sign-off after 2-week evaluation
[08:55] Aisha Khan: That aligns with our expectations. can we add a quality monitoring plan? we'd like rolling regressions alerts
[09:03] Liam O'Connor: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and regression alerts — we can tie alerts to your eval prompt set and push notifications to Slack or PagerDuty
[09:15] Carlos Ramirez: For alerting, we need a way to roll back to a previous model variant if quality drops
[09:22] Sofia Patel: We support rollouts with canary and automatic fallback policies. SE will set up a rollout plan in the deep-dive
[09:34] Emily Nguyen: Any blockers from your side to start the hosted pilot with de-identified data?
[09:40] Jordan Miles: Need legal ok on the TOS and a quick BAA for the pilot — Emily will coordinate with legal
[09:48] Maya Chen: I'll drop the legal pack and the BAA request in the follow-up email. and we'll put a note about de-id for pilot datasets
[10:05] Sofia Patel: Now a quick tech note on performance: for lower latency we recommend shorter context windows and a quantized model profile. Liam will propose quantization & batching settings

[10:18] Liam O'Connor: Yep, we'll look at your sequence length distribution and tune kernels accordingly. expect recommendations like micro-batching 8-16 requests depending on the model and target latency
[10:33] Carlos Ramirez: Are there any restrictions on model size for Private deployments? we have limited GPU capacity on-prem
[10:39] Liam O'Connor: We have quantization-friendly execution paths and smaller variants that run well on limited GPUs. we'll recommend a model/quant profile based on your throughput needs
[10:52] Aisha Khan: For the pilot success evaluation, are we going to do both accuracy and human review?
[10:58] Maya Chen: We recommend a hybrid: automated metrics on the eval set plus a human review sample for edge cases. Redwood Optimize can help with drift detection
[11:10] Jordan Miles: Ok — timeline recap? we wanted a pilot in 4 weeks. if we get the checklist and eval set in 3 days, can you spin up hosted test env quickly?
[11:20] Sofia Patel: Yes if we receive the eval set and legal sign-off quickly, hosted pilot can start within a week. Private will take longer due to network & security approvals
[11:33] Emily Nguyen: I'll aim to get the eval sample and legal intro by 2027-04-06. any blockers we should know about?
[11:40] Maya Chen: None from Redwood side — only the usual legal and network approvals. we'll help chase internally
[11:52] Carlos Ramirez: For the deep-dive, can we include our infra architect? he'll want to discuss peering and firewall specifics
[12:00] Liam O'Connor: Definitely. We'll include a checklist for network ports and CIDR ranges. also we'll provide a staging test harness for latency testing
[12:14] Aisha Khan: One concern — cost tradeoffs: if we go Dedicated, what's the minimum commit and typical ROI timeline?

[12:22] Sofia Patel: Dedicated commits vary; typical deals start with a monthly reserved capacity. ROI depends on volume — we'll include example math in the pricing doc. for many customers it pays for itself in 3-6 months with batching and cache
[12:39] Jordan Miles: Sounds reasonable. any final open questions from customers?
[12:46] Emily Nguyen: None here. just recap and timelines please

[12:52] Sofia Patel: Recap — Redwood to send: onboarding checklist, security/legal pack, eval prompt template, and pricing sheet. SE to schedule deep-dive and prepare benchmark plan. Customer to send eval set, network diagram, and confirm pilot participants. we aim to start pilot in ~4 weeks. action items and due dates recorded
[13:18] Maya Chen: i'll include next steps and action items in the follow-up email, plus links to docs and the SOC2 request form
[13:26] Jordan Miles: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity. we'll look out for the docs
[13:31] Sofia Patel: Thanks, talk soon — we'll send follow-up by end of day
[57:30] Meeting ended
